title: Enterprise deal forecast signoff and revenue trigger guide
author: Eleanor Zhao
content:
Overview

This document defines the operational workflow and decision criteria that link enterprise deal signoff, quarterly forecasts, contract milestones, and the revenue recognition / billing trigger events used by Finance, Sales Operations, Legal, and Revenue Engineering. It is intended for the teams listed in Scope and should be used whenever a deal meets the Enterprise Deal definition (see Scope).

Scope

- Applies to: all enterprise contracts (annual committed revenue >= $250k or complex procurement/legal terms such as escrow, data residency, or customer-hosted deployment).
- Excludes: self-serve and SMB deals (handled via standard billing platform workflows).

Definitions

- Forecast Signoff: formal acceptance by Finance and Revenue Operations that a committed opportunity is eligible to be included in the quarterly revenue forecast.
- Rev Trigger: the contractual or operational event that initiates revenue recognition and/or first invoicing (e.g., service acceptance, delivery milestone, go-live date, or effective date).

Roles & responsibilities

- Finance (Revenue Accounting): owns revenue recognition policy interpretation, approves rev trigger class, and creates recognition schedules in ERP.
- Sales Operations: ensures CRM/opportunity metadata is accurate (contract type, billing cadence, rev trigger candidate, legal approval status).
- Legal: approves contractual language and confirms binding effective date and any conditions precedent.
- Sales (AE/AM): obtains customer signoff, finalizes SOW/MSA countersignature, and submits procurement artifacts.
- RevOps / Billing: configures billing schedules and test invoices; coordinates billing cutover.

Quarterly forecast signoff workflow (numbered checklist)

1) Opportunity gating (Sales Ops)
   1.1 Confirm opportunity stage is "Contracting" or "Closed - Pending" and total contract value (TCV) >= $250k.
   1.2 Attach final contract, SOW, and procurement PO (if available) into the CRM record.

2) Legal review (Legal)
   2.1 Confirm MSA/SOW executed by authorized signatories; note any outstanding conditions precedent.
   2.2 If escrow/kms/data-residency clauses present, attach legal exception ticket and ETA for remediation.

3) Rev trigger classification (Finance + Legal + Sales Ops)
   3.1 Evaluate which of the standard rev triggers applies: Effective date, Delivery milestone acceptance, Customer go-live, or Usage-based threshold.
   3.2 If non-standard rev trigger is proposed, document risk and obtain Revenue Accounting signoff.

4) Forecast inclusion (Finance)
   4.1 Finance validates recognition schedule and confirms inclusion for the quarter when the rev trigger is expected to occur.
   4.2 Signoff captured via the Forecast Signoff spreadsheet and a stamped CRM field: "ForecastApprovedByFinance = true".

5) Billing readiness (RevOps)
   5.1 Ensure billing account exists, billing contact and tax details are captured, and payment terms are setup.
   5.2 Create test invoice and validate numeric mapping to contract line items.

Contract-to-Rev trigger matrix (use as a decision table)

| Contract pattern | Typical rev trigger | Required artifacts for signoff | Standard accounting treatment |
|------------------|---------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------------------|
| MSA + SOW (no delivery dependencies) | Effective date (signed) | Fully executed MSA + SOW | Recognize over subscription term (ratable) |
| SOW with delivery milestone(s) | Customer acceptance of milestone | Acceptance certificate, milestone report | Recognize on acceptance (milestone accounting) |
| On-prem / private deployment | Go-live / handover to customer | Deployment checklist, handover signoff | May require deferred revenue until acceptance |
| Usage-based pricing | Threshold met / first billable usage | Usage report, billing extract | Recognize as billed (variable consideration rules) |
| Trials / Pilot -> Enterprise | Conversion acceptance | Signed conversion amendment | Recognize from conversion effective date |

Billing cutover and invoicing checklist (operational playbook)

- 7 business days before expected rev trigger:
  - Confirm CRM > Billing alignment and contract mapping.
  - Create draft invoice in staging billing environment.
  - Confirm taxation and VAT handling with Tax Ops.
- 3 business days before expected rev trigger:
  - Legal to confirm no outstanding signature or CPs.
  - Finance to confirm recognition schedule entry created.
- Day 0 (rev trigger day):
  - Execute invoice run (RevOps), validate amounts, and send invoice to customer.
  - Upload invoice copy and recognition schedule into the contract folder.
- 3 business days after Day 0:
  - Revenue Accounting reconcilies invoice to recognition schedule and confirms posting.

Escalation & exception handling

- If Legal has open exceptions that change the rev trigger, Sales Ops must open a Forecast Exception ticket in JIRA (label: rev-trigger-exception) with owner and ETA.
- For disputes that block invoicing >10 business days past rev trigger, trigger the Revenue Hold escalation: notify VP Finance, General Counsel, and CRO.
- All exceptions must be reviewed in the monthly Revenue Governance meeting.

Artifacts & templates (links and code snippets)

- Forecast signoff template (use this as the canonical sheet): 
  - Columns: OpportunityID, Account, TCV, ContractType, RevTrigger, ExpectedTriggerDate, ForecastQuarter, FinanceSignoff, LegalSignoff, BillingReady.

- Contract metadata JSON (to be attached to CRM record):

  {
    "opportunity_id": "OPP-12345",
    "contract_type": "MSA+SOW",
    "tcv": "550000",
    "currency": "USD",
    "rev_trigger": "effective_date",
    "trigger_date": "2026-02-01",
    "billing_cadence": "annual",
    "billing_contact": "finance@customer.com"
  }

Operational controls and thresholds

- Material contract threshold (requires senior finance review): TCV >= $1.5M or multi-year > 36 months.
- Revenue recognition policy exceptions: any clause that defers recognition beyond 90 days from effective date must be routed to Revenue Accounting for policy review.
- Billing hold threshold: disputes > $50k trigger immediate VP-level notification.

Monitoring and monthly governance

- Revenue Governance meeting cadence: monthly, chaired by Director of Revenue Accounting. Agenda includes: forecast accuracy review, open rev-trigger exceptions, and high-risk deals.
- Key metrics monitored:
  - Forecast accuracy (actual vs. forecasted recognized revenue) by deal cohort.
  - Time-to-invoice (days between rev trigger and first invoice).
  - Exception aging (days open).
